name: Ame no Oshihomimi
summary:
Ame no Oshihomimi (天忍穗耳尊, 天之忍穂耳命), known by his regnal name Amaterasu Ōmikami, was the first son of the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Omikami and her husband Nunokagutsuhiko. Born in the late 10th century BCE in Yamato, Nippon (modern-day Japan), he played a pivotal role in shaping the mythology of the Japanese imperial family.

As the successor to his mother's divine authority, Ame no Oshihomimi became the first emperor of the Yamato state, uniting various clans and tribes under his rule. His reign marked the beginning of the Imperial Era in Japan, which would last for centuries.

Ame no Oshihomimi is also revered as a symbol of the divine power of the imperial family, with his name appearing in the oldest surviving Japanese texts, the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki. His legacy continues to influence Japanese culture and politics to this day.

The significance of Ame no Oshihomimi's reign lies in its role in establishing the mythology of the Japanese imperial family, which has shaped the country's history, politics, and identity. He is remembered as a unifying figure who brought order and stability to a region torn apart by conflict and disunity.

In conclusion, Ame no Oshihomimi's impact on Japanese history cannot be overstated. His reign marked the beginning of a new era in Japanese culture and politics, one that would be shaped by his divine authority and his role as the first emperor of the Yamato state.
